title: Strengthen to pairwise non-distinctness, then convert to the card bound (IMO 2025 P1)
intent: Prove that a non-sunny line (slope l.1 ≠ 0 and ≠ −1) meets the boundary of the triangular lattice-point set in at most two points, by first strengthening the goal to the pairwise statement 'any three points of the filtered set have two equal' (non_sunny_lines_cover_at_most_2_points_on_boundary_h_main), then converting that to the cardinality bound ≤ 2 (non_sunny_lines_cover_at_most_2_points_on_boundary_h_final).
also_known_as: reformulate a cardinality bound as pairwise non-distinctness

parent.name: non_sunny_lines_cover_at_most_2_points_on_boundary
parent.statement:
theorem non_sunny_lines_cover_at_most_2_points_on_boundary (n k : ℕ) (verts : Finset ℝ) (lines : Finset (ℝ × ℝ)) (points : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hcard : lines.card + verts.card = n) (hallpoints : ∀ p, p ∈ points ↔ p.1 ≥ 1 ∧ p.2 ≥ 1 ∧ p.1 + p.2 ≤ n + 1) (hmain : ∀ p ∈ points, (∃ l ∈ lines, l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2) ∨ (∃ x ∈ verts, p.1 = x)) (hk : (lines.filter (fun l ↦ l.1 ≠ 0 ∧ l.1 ≠ -1)).card = k) (l : ℝ × ℝ) (h_non_sunny : l.1 ≠ 0 ∧ l.1 ≠ -1) :
  (Finset.filter (fun p ↦ (p.1 = 1 ∨ p.2 = 1 ∨ p.1 + p.2 = n + 1) ∧
    (l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2)) points).card ≤ 2

children.name: non_sunny_lines_cover_at_most_2_points_on_boundary_h_main
children.statement:
lemma non_sunny_lines_cover_at_most_2_points_on_boundary_h_main (n k : ℕ)
  (verts : Finset ℝ)
  (lines : Finset (ℝ × ℝ))
  (points : Finset (ℕ × ℕ))
  (hn : 3 ≤ n)
  (hcard : lines.card + verts.card = n)
  (hallpoints : ∀ p, p ∈ points ↔ p.1 ≥ 1 ∧ p.2 ≥ 1 ∧ p.1 + p.2 ≤ n + 1)
  (hmain : ∀ p ∈ points, (∃ l ∈ lines, l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2) ∨ (∃ x ∈ verts, p.1 = x))
  (hk : (lines.filter (fun l ↦ l.1 ≠ 0 ∧ l.1 ≠ -1)).card = k)
  (l : ℝ × ℝ)
  (h_non_sunny : l.1 ≠ 0 ∧ l.1 ≠ -1):
  ∀ (x y z : ℕ × ℕ), x ∈ (Finset.filter (fun p ↦ (p.1 = 1 ∨ p.2 = 1 ∨ p.1 + p.2 = n + 1) ∧ (l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2)) points) → y ∈ (Finset.filter (fun p ↦ (p.1 = 1 ∨ p.2 = 1 ∨ p.1 + p.2 = n + 1) ∧ (l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2)) points) → z ∈ (Finset.filter (fun p ↦ (p.1 = 1 ∨ p.2 = 1 ∨ p.1 + p.2 = n + 1) ∧ (l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2)) points) → x = y ∨ x = z ∨ y = z
children.closed_by: the 3×3×3 rcases on x.1 = 1 ∨ x.2 = 1 ∨ x.1 + x.2 = n + 1 (and the same for y and z); each leaf closes with same_boundary_condition_implies_eq (two points on one boundary are equal, then tauto) or contradiction_from_conditions (exfalso, when the three points sit on the three distinct boundaries)
children.note: The strengthened statement: any three points of the filtered set have two equal (no three distinct points). The hard half of the proof, a case analysis on which boundary condition each of x, y, z satisfies.

children.name: non_sunny_lines_cover_at_most_2_points_on_boundary_h_final
children.statement:
lemma non_sunny_lines_cover_at_most_2_points_on_boundary_h_final (n k : ℕ)
  (verts : Finset ℝ)
  (lines : Finset (ℝ × ℝ))
  (points : Finset (ℕ × ℕ))
  (hn : 3 ≤ n)
  (hcard : lines.card + verts.card = n)
  (hallpoints : ∀ p, p ∈ points ↔ p.1 ≥ 1 ∧ p.2 ≥ 1 ∧ p.1 + p.2 ≤ n + 1)
  (hmain : ∀ p ∈ points, (∃ l ∈ lines, l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2) ∨ (∃ x ∈ verts, p.1 = x))
  (hk : (lines.filter (fun l ↦ l.1 ≠ 0 ∧ l.1 ≠ -1)).card = k)
  (l : ℝ × ℝ)
  (h_non_sunny : l.1 ≠ 0 ∧ l.1 ≠ -1)
  (h_main : ∀ (x y z : ℕ × ℕ), x ∈ (Finset.filter (fun p ↦ (p.1 = 1 ∨ p.2 = 1 ∨ p.1 + p.2 = n + 1) ∧ (l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2)) points) → y ∈ (Finset.filter (fun p ↦ (p.1 = 1 ∨ p.2 = 1 ∨ p.1 + p.2 = n + 1) ∧ (l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2)) points) → z ∈ (Finset.filter (fun p ↦ (p.1 = 1 ∨ p.2 = 1 ∨ p.1 + p.2 = n + 1) ∧ (l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2)) points) → x = y ∨ x = z ∨ y = z):
  (Finset.filter (fun p ↦ (p.1 = 1 ∨ p.2 = 1 ∨ p.1 + p.2 = n + 1) ∧ (l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2)) points).card ≤ 2
children.closed_by: by_contra h, then the finite-set fact that card > 2 gives three distinct elements (the have h₄ … exact? step), rcases to x, y, z, then have h₃ := h_main x y z hx hy hz; tauto
children.note: The conversion: a finite set with more than two elements contains three pairwise distinct elements, which contradicts h_main, so the cardinality is at most 2. The generic half, independent of the geometry.

applicability.goal_shape: A finite-set cardinality bound (Finset.filter P s).card ≤ 2, where P is a conjunction of a disjunctive boundary condition (p.1 = 1 ∨ p.2 = 1 ∨ p.1 + p.2 = n + 1) and a line-membership equation (l.1 * p.1 + l.2 = p.2).
applicability.use_when: The bound is hard to reach by counting the filter directly, but the equivalent 'no three distinct elements' statement is exactly what a case analysis on the boundary condition can show, and the conversion from 'no three distinct' to 'card ≤ 2' is a generic finite-set fact (here filled by exact?).
applicability.avoid_when: The target cardinality is not equivalent to pairwise non-distinctness (a bound of 1, or a bound over an infinite set or a multiset); or the pairwise statement does not split more cleanly than the original — here it does because the boundary disjunction gives finitely many cases, each a linear equation in the slope l.1.

consequences: Splits the goal into a strengthened statement (h_main, the hard case analysis) and a generic conversion (h_final, from pairwise non-distinctness to card ≤ 2). The two halves must meet exactly: h_final's hypothesis h_main is verbatim h_main's conclusion, and the glue passes it unchanged. The equivalence relies on the set being finite (a Finset) so that 'no three distinct elements' is exactly 'card ≤ 2'.
